name: Battle of Alesia

phases.title: Two lines of fortification round Alesia
phases.text: Caesar shut the Gauls into Alesia and built two lines of works, one facing the town and one facing outwards against a relief force. The Roman lines, with a camp of two legions on a hill beside them, stood ready.

phases.title: The relief force and the besieged attack together
phases.text: The relief force arrived and attacked the outer line while the besieged Gauls attacked the inner line at the same moment. The combined attack failed.

phases.title: A night attack fails and the Gauls withdraw
phases.text: The Gauls attacked again at night. The relief force withdrew at first light for fear of being surrounded, and the besieged, delayed by filling the Roman trenches, returned to the town.

phases.title: Sixty thousand Gauls attack the weak camp
phases.text: The Gauls chose a weak point where a camp of two legions stood on bad ground and sent 60,000 men against it, attacking at noon. Vercingetorix sallied against the inner line at the same time.

phases.title: Labienus and Caesar come to the weak point
phases.text: Caesar sent Labienus to support the weak area, then led fresh troops there himself. The attack on the inner line was repelled.

phases.title: Roman cavalry takes the Gauls in the rear
phases.text: Part of the Roman cavalry left the outer line and appeared at the rear of the Gauls. The Roman troops advanced rapidly, the Gauls fled, and the cavalry intercepted them. The besieged Gauls were pulled back from the fortification.

note: The plan shows the whole operation, not a single field: armies and fortification lines round Alesia. The accounts give no compass directions, so the layout is schematic. Both fortification lines are drawn as open outlines (the real lines were not continuous). The relief force is drawn on the east, outside the outer line, and the hill with the weak camp on the north-east; the accounts do not say on which side of the town they lay. Labienus's six cohorts are described as cavalry. The Roman cavalry's path is drawn straight; its route is not given. The siege lasted a month and the fighting several days, so no single date is shown.
